_policy: Every continue-on-error in a workflow carries a disposition: ratchet (a number that may not rise), expires (a date by which someone must decide again), or conditional (soft here, hard somewhere that matters). Enforced by scripts/check-gate-policy.py. Reasoning: docs/testing/gaps.md G3/G4.

ci.yml::frontend-lint-type-test::Audit f.why: Same as the Python audit, and additionally noisy because the full audit includes dev deps like Vite that never ship.

ci.yml::gates.why: Job-level `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.soft == true }}`, and mypy is the only cell that sets it. Same disposition it had as a step before the 3 Sep split into a fail-fast:false matrix — 238 errors is a project, not a commit, so the count is held instead. If a second cell is ever marked soft, this single key stops describing it and the entry must be split.

ci.yml::supply-chain::Audit dependencies.why: Upstream CVEs are not ours to fix on demand, so a failure here is news rather than a defect. The date is the next quarterly dep review; the decision then is whether anything found has sat unaddressed.

ci.yml::supply-chain::Generate Python SB.why: Artifact generation, not a correctness check: a failure means no SBOM was published, which matters for the verifiable-security-claim track and nothing else. Revisit when that track needs the SBOM to be reliable.

ci.yml::test.hard_when: release.yml calls ci.yml with strict-macos: true
ci.yml::test.why: The best pattern in the tree and the model for the rest: the same suite is informational on a push and blocking on a tag, so cost is paid where it buys something. Needs no expiry — it is already hard where it counts.
